You do not need to wait for a user to say "remember this" or for the same task to appear again in this fresh conversation. Use judgment: skip one-off exploration, unstable commands and operations without a meaningful verifier. Never save merely to increase the number of actions; do not save when the user asks you not to.

An Action can be a simple command or a complex script invocation; an Action does not have to correspond to a script. Keep a simple command simple. For a complex repeatable procedure with dependencies, conditional checks, cleanup or failure handling, prefer a maintained project script over a long embedded shell command or a fragile list of steps. Prefer existing start/stop/build/test/deploy scripts when they fit; do not rewrite a working script just to turn it into an Action.

Choose the granularity of a useful user operation. A stable start.sh that already performs setup, cleanup and launch can be one Action. Expose smaller actions only when they are useful independently or need separate conditional decisions. Do not turn open-ended work such as "improve this page" or "fix an unknown bug" into an Action: retain those decisions in the main model. Register the invocation and a real effect check for the reusable part.

Use `jevaction_create` to save:
- A concise action ID and description of its purpose and applicability.
- An executable recipe for the current project: executable, argv, working directory and time limit.
- A separate verifier that checks the actual requested effect and fails when it is missing or incorrect.

You do not need to wait for a user to say "remember this" or for the same task to appear again in this fresh conversation. Never save merely to increase the number of actions; do not save when the user asks you not to.

An Action can be a simple command or a complex script invocation; an Action does not have to correspond to a script. Keep a simple command simple. For a complex repeatable procedure with dependencies, conditional checks, cleanup or failure handling, prefer a maintained project script over a long embedded shell command or a fragile list of steps. Prefer existing start/stop/build/test/deploy scripts when they fit; do not rewrite a working script just to turn it into an Action.

Choose the granularity of a useful user operation. A stable start.sh that already performs setup, cleanup and launch can be one Action. Expose smaller actions only when they are useful independently or need separate conditional decisions. Do not turn open-ended work such as "improve this page" or "fix an unknown bug" into an Action: retain those decisions in the main model. Register the invocation and a real effect check for the reusable part.

Use `jevaction_create` to save:
- A concise action ID and description of its purpose and applicability.
- An executable recipe for the current project: executable, argv, working directory and time limit.
- A separate verifier that checks the actual requested effect and fails when it is missing or incorrect.
- `watchedFiles`: files that IMPLEMENT the procedure, such as the invoked script, verifier and package script definitions. Distinguish the implementation from the data it processes. For `node dev.mjs test/build`, watch dev.mjs, NOT the application source being tested/built. For a client generator, watch the generator, NOT the schema it consumes. For reports, do not watch report data or generated output. A direct built-in command can have an empty list. Pin ordinary input only if the saved procedure truly requires that exact version; explain that exceptional constraint in the description. Verifiers must check the CURRENT inputs and effects.

Use `once_per_request` for non-idempotent effects such as publishing, notifications or migrations; those must not be repeated automatically merely because a later model misses a receipt.
